title: Grade 6 Science — Fri, Jun 20
description: Changes Around Us — Day 5 of 5: Mixed review
subject: science

questions.question: Which is a physical change?
questions.explanation: Cutting cloth only changes shape and size — no new substance is formed. It is a physical change.

questions.question: Which is a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Burning paper produces ash and gases — new substances. It is an irreversible chemical change.

questions.question: Rusting requires both ___ and ___.
questions.explanation: Rusting occurs when iron is in the presence of both water (moisture) and oxygen.

questions.question: Cooking an egg is ___.
questions.explanation: Heat causes irreversible chemical changes in egg protein. The egg cannot be 'uncooked.'

questions.question: Which is a reversible change?
questions.explanation: Melting ice is reversible — water can be frozen back into ice. The others are irreversible.

questions.question: Galvanizing coats iron with ___.
questions.explanation: Galvanization involves coating iron with zinc to prevent rusting.

questions.question: Formation of a new substance is the key sign of a ___ change.
questions.explanation: Chemical changes produce one or more new substances with different properties — the key identifying feature.

questions.question: Stretching a rubber band is a ___.
questions.explanation: Stretching rubber is a physical change — when released, the rubber returns to its original shape. It is reversible.

questions.question: Painting iron prevents rusting by ___.
options: Blocking water and oxygen from reaching iron
questions.explanation: Paint creates a physical barrier that prevents water and oxygen (the two requirements for rusting) from reaching iron.

questions.question: Dissolving salt in water is a ___ change.
questions.explanation: Salt dissolves physically in water. No new substance is formed. The salt can be recovered by evaporation.

questions.question: Which change is irreversible?
questions.explanation: Fermentation is a chemical change — yeast converts sugar in grape juice to alcohol. This cannot be reversed.

questions.question: Iron does NOT rust if ___.
options: Kept in dry air without moisture
questions.explanation: Without moisture (water), rusting cannot occur. Dry air provides no water for the rusting reaction.

questions.question: Rusting is an example of ___.
questions.explanation: Rusting produces iron oxide (a new chemical substance) — chemical change. It cannot easily be reversed — irreversible.

questions.question: A reversible change is generally a ___ change.
questions.explanation: Reversible changes are generally physical — they change form or state without forming new substances.

questions.question: Which of these produces light, heat, AND new substances?
questions.explanation: Burning coal produces light, heat, carbon dioxide and ash — new substances — confirming it is an irreversible chemical change.
